blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Bhopal Gas Tragedy occurred in 1984, representing one of MP's critical modern historical events.
Simhastha Kumbh Mela is celebrated in Ujjain along the banks of the sacred Kshipra river.
Madhya Pradesh is recognized as the 'Soybean State' of India due to its vast production.
Rewa region is historically famous for its connection to white tigers.
Ken-Betwa River Interlinking Project is a major infrastructure initiative connecting key rivers in the region.
Madhya Pradesh hosts numerous ancient temples of significant architectural and cultural value.

blocks.content: The Bhopal Gas Tragedy occurred on the night of 2-3 December 1984 at the Union Carbide India Limited (UCIL) pesticide plant in Bhopal. Methyl Isocyanate (MIC) gas leaked from the plant, causing immediate deaths of thousands and long-term health impacts affecting hundreds of thousands of people. It is considered the world's worst industrial disaster. The tragedy led to significant changes in industrial safety regulations in India and globally. Warren Anderson was the CEO of Union Carbide at the time of the tragedy. The Indian government passed the Bhopal Gas Leak (Processing of Claims) Act, 1985 to handle compensation claims.

Ujjain is one of the four locations (along with Prayagraj, Haridwar, and Nashik) where the Kumbh Mela is held. At Ujjain, it is called Simhastha because it is held when Jupiter (Brihaspati) enters the Leo (Simha) zodiac sign. Kumbh at Ujjain is held every 12 years on the banks of the sacred Kshipra River. The most recent Simhastha was held in 2016 and the next will be held in 2028.

Madhya Pradesh produces more than 60% of India's total soybean output, making it the undisputed 'Soybean Capital' of India. Soybean is a Kharif crop grown mainly in the black cotton soil (regur) areas of Malwa Plateau. Major producing districts include Indore, Ujjain, Dewas, Mandsaur, Shajapur, and Agar-Malwa. Soybean has transformed the agricultural economy of western MP. The crop is used for oil extraction, protein meal, and various processed food products.

The first white tiger in modern times was discovered in Rewa district of Madhya Pradesh. Maharaja Martand Singh of Rewa captured a white tiger cub named Mohan in 1951 from the jungles of Rewa. Mohan became the progenitor of most white tigers seen in zoos worldwide today. The white coloration in tigers is due to a recessive gene. White tigers are not a separate species but rather a color variant of Bengal Tigers.

items: Bhopal Gas Tragedy (1984) and associated facts are frequently tested in MPPSC general studies.
Simhastha Kumbh Mela details, including its 12-year cycle and Ujjain location on the Kshipra River, are key exam topics.
Ken-Betwa river linking project details are crucial for geography and current affairs sections.

blocks.content: The Ken-Betwa River Interlinking Project is the first river interlinking project in India. It involves transferring surplus water from the Ken River (Panna region) to the water-deficient Betwa River basin. The project aims to provide irrigation to the drought-prone areas of Bundelkhand in both Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. However, the project has been controversial because it involves diversion of water through the Panna Tiger Reserve, potentially affecting the tiger habitat.
